thread:
maria chen: Heads up, I'm seeing a reproducible correctness regression with activation quant + mixed-precision matmul when batching across KV cache boundaries.

jon lin: details? env, model, steps?

maria chen: small repro on dev-gpu-2: running long-chat workload with fp8 kernel selected after calibration. If a request crosses a cached KV boundary and the runtime switches kernel mid-batch, outputs diverge (checksum mismatch) ~20% of the time.

kevin rao: what do you mean by "switches kernel mid-batch"? we only pick kernel per-op right?

maria chen: yes but kernel selection is dynamic: we pick fp8 vs bf16 based on live calibration stats and sequence-length distribution. In this case calibration triggers a kernel switch after the first few tokens of a batched request. KV cache slices end up with mismatched scale metadata.

perf-bot: perf report uploaded: https://internal/reports/1830123456

maria chen: logs:
```
[2026-03-15 14:22:03] INFO kernel_selector: selected=fp8_matmul_v2 (scale=0.0213)
[2026-03-15 14:22:03] INFO kv_cache: store: offset=0 len=4096 scale_meta=0.0213
[2026-03-15 14:22:04] INFO kernel_selector: switched=bf16_matmul (no-scale)
ERROR checksum mismatch: layer3 activation != expected (delta 0.0021)
```

jon lin: repro script? can you paste command?

maria chen: yeah:
```
python -m tests.run_perf --model redwood-7b-mix --mode streaming --batch 4 --seq 2048 --calib live --seed 42
```

kevin rao: interesting. nvprof shows a kernel id flip between launches for the same op when batch contains boundary crossing. Could be kernel_selector not respecting per-request scale metadata during batching merge.

maria chen: hypothesis: when we coalesce requests for continuous batching we merge KV pointers but we don't consistently propagate the per-request activation scale or a race updates the shared scale table.

ops-bot: deploy-note: staging runtime bumped to runtime-1.12.2 at 14:05 UTC (contains dynamic-kernel refactor)

jon lin: i can reproduce within 10 runs on staging. Will instrument kernel_selector to log request-id -> kernel mapping and KV metadata pointers.

maria chen: thanks. also saw weirdness where prefix cache_from=1 and cache_from=0 requests in same batch produced different scale_meta but the merged call used the older scale header.

kevin rao: probable root causes:
- batching heuristics merge per-request metadata incorrectly
- kernel switch path doesn't replay per-request calibrations for cached KV slices
- scale table updates are not atomic w.r.t. batch dispatch

perf-bot: quick profile snippet from staging (truncated):
```
kernel launch sequence: fp8_v2, fp8_v2, bf16, bf16
kv write offsets: 0, 4096, 8192, 12288
scale table at launch: [0.0213, 0.0213, null, null]
```

jon lin: plan:
1) add guarded copy of per-request scale metadata during batch coalescing (short PR)
2) add assert in dev builds to verify scale_meta for each KV slice at matmul entry
3) add regression test that mixes cache_from=1/0 and forces kernel switches

maria chen: I'll open the regression test and upload failing artifacts under /mnt/eval/1830123456

kevin rao: I'll audit kernel_selector's stateful objects for non-threadsafe mutations. If true, we should treat scale table as immutable snapshot per-batch.

jon lin: quick debugging note: you can trigger error more reliably by lowering calib threshold: --calib-threshold 0.02 and seed 7.

maria chen: thanks. assigning: jon -> repro + short PR (#TBD), kevin -> audit + design fix, i'll own the regression test and rollback plan. Will coordinate canary in dedicated cluster after fix.

ops-bot: ticket created: INF-2147 "activation-quant scale race when batching across KV boundaries" (link: https://internal/issue/INF-2147)

maria chen: tagged INF-2147 in the PR when ready. FYI this seems orthogonal to matmul numerical kernel math itself — it's the metadata alignment between KV cache entries and kernel selection/codepath.

jon lin: ok I'll start with minimal guardians and the dev assert so we get a noisy signal in CI.

kevin rao: if that works, we should also add a unit test in kernel_selector that simulates interleaved updates and validates snapshot semantics.

maria chen: thanks everyone. I'll post repro artifacts and a short flamegraph once I have the coveralls. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: nightly alert: added regression watcher for INF-2147 to watch test suite for 24h

jon lin: logging note: include request-id and batch-coalesced-id in the kernel headers, otherwise triage is painful.

maria chen: agreed. final note — watch out for mixed cache_from flags; that's the most reliable trigger here. ending triage for now, will update thread with PR link.
